newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods steady late with few players.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods steady late with few players.

text.p: U.S. West Coast products prices were mostly steady in razor-thin late trade, with most traders attending an industry function and NYMEX falling.
NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures closed at 62.20 cents a gallon, down 2.40 cents from Friday as the October contract went off the boards.
And while Unocal Corp said it restarted a hydrogen unit at its Rodeo, Calif., refinery, traders speculated that shut unit may have caused further problems downstream.
"Hydrogen is a pretty important commodity to a cracker," one trader said, noting gasoline supplies could drop.
Hydrogen helps to remove sulphur from diesel in the gasoline-making process.
Rumors of the problem lifted Bay-area gasoline Friday from nearly three cents under Los Angeles to parity with L.A.
As forecast, middle distillates eased early on rumours that the U.S. military changed who it granted jet fuel contracts to.
But trade quieted in the afternoon, with bids for jet fuel in Los Angeles unchanged at 71 cents a gallon, and offers at 72 cents.
Low sulphur, or "EPA" diesel, was flat Monday at 70/71 cents a gallon after tailing off last week.

San Francisco distillates edged up about a cent from late last week to hit a one cent premium over L.A.. Values rose as demand from harvest equipment in northern California began to eat into supplies.
L.A. CARB gasoline remained notionally unchanged at 71/73 cents, with a deal done Friday at 73 cents.
Wholesale prices for conventional regular gasoline in Los Angeles stayed 65/66 cents Monday.
